# SEAL

SEAL is coming to the Mac App Store first. Source and direct downloads will follow later.
Agent, terminal, MCP, and CLI guides describe source and direct-edition tools.

- [Edition differences](docs/editions.html): Store features and direct-edition recordings.

- [Support](support.html): contact information and problem-reporting instructions.

> SEAL is a local-first macOS workbench for sequences, lab records, and activity records. A separately built Rust CLI and source-checkout MCP server can work against the same SQLite workspace as the desktop app.

This file indexes SEAL's documentation for coding agents. SEAL is a local-first macOS workbench for DNA, RNA, and protein. Use an authorized source checkout to build the app, or install a verified unnotarized DMG when the repository has a release. A Mac App Store edition is planned. MCP requires a separate source checkout and an explicit active workspace path. Use block_list for shared sequence blocks; workspace_list covers MCP Scratch only. The Sample Lab includes synthetic examples. Network services run when requested; the app sends no telemetry.

## Get started
- [Overview](docs/index.html): What SEAL is and how the docs are organized.
- [Install SEAL](docs/install.html): Build from source, install an available GitHub DMG, or read about the planned Mac App Store edition.
- [Quickstart](docs/quickstart.html): From a pasted sequence to a first analysis in a few minutes.
- [Core concepts](docs/concepts.html): Workspaces, Entries, stable conversation API names, blocks, features, and the sequence model.
- [Sequence sources](docs/sequence-sources.html): Synthetic fixtures, your own files, explicit public-database fetches, and provenance.

## Sequence workflows
- [Import and export](docs/import-export.html): Read eleven file formats, write FASTA, GenBank, and GFF3.
- [Editing and annotation](docs/editing.html): Edit bases, add features, and annotate selections.
- [Plasmid maps](docs/plasmid-map.html): Open any block as a circular or linear map with feature lanes and cut sites.
- [Restriction digest](docs/restriction-digest.html): Map and simulate cuts across 154 enzymes.
- [Primer design](docs/primer-design.html): Design and rank PCR primers with Tm and clamp checks.
- [Cloning and assembly](docs/cloning.html): Plan Gibson, Golden Gate, GoldenBraid, MoClo, ligation, and guided clone builds.
- [Sequence alignment](docs/alignment.html): Pairwise and multiple alignment with selectable engines.
- [Sanger traces](docs/sanger-traces.html): Import AB1 chromatograms and read per-base quality.
- [Translation and ORFs](docs/translation.html): Live selection translation, all six frames, reverse-translation drafts, and ORFs.
- [Protein analysis](docs/protein-analysis.html): Molecular weight, charge, hydropathy, annotations, and predictions.
- [Codon analysis](docs/codon-analysis.html): Codon usage, GC content, and host comparison.
- [Sequence diff](docs/diff.html): Compare two sequences base by base.
- [Quality checks](docs/quality.html): Flag homopolymers, ambiguous bases, and internal stops.
- [Reports and packages](docs/reports.html): Export reports and zipped packages.

## Design and generation
- [ESM design](docs/esm-design.html): Generate, insert, and mutate sequences with the biohub.ai ESM engine.
- [Codon optimizers](docs/codon-optimizers.html): Optimize coding sequences with pluggable host profiles.
- [CRISPR guide design](docs/guide-design.html): Design guides for a region and scan a chosen reference for off-target sites.

## Notebook
- [Notebook](docs/notebook.html): A local lab notebook whose pages reference the sequences they describe.
- [Records and signing](docs/notebook-records.html): Revisions, restore points, signing a page, and what the attestation covers.
